chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Mufrid (or Qarin) who drives his sacrificial animal with him, upon him is two circumambulations (Tawaf) around the House and one Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, and it is appropriate for him to stipulate to his Lord: if it is not a Hajj, then it is an Umrah.
And from the conditions of the Qarin is that he drives his camel with him, and shears its hair from its right side, and adorns it with a sandal which he has prayed in, and he narrated that.

key_terms.اَلْقَارِنُ: One who combines Hajj and Umrah

ai.seo_question: What are the ritual obligations and conditions for a Qarin in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the ritual precision required for the Qarin, a pilgrim who performs Hajj and Umrah together, emphasizing the necessity of two circumambulations (Tawaf) and a single Sa'i. It further highlights the symbolic act of adorning the sacrificial animal with the pilgrim’s sandal, reflecting the deep integration of personal devotion with ritual sacrifice in Shia fiqh. The condition to stipulate if the Hajj is not accepted underscores the theological importance of intention (Niyyah) in validating the pilgrimage.
